text: Two white surfaces. That is all you get. I had a third one, but it was being used to hold up the ceiling.
The far side is twenty one metres away. I did not measure it with a subject this time. I measured it with a falling subject. The results were similar.
You have tried it once and arrived in the acid. You are welcome to keep the same plan and hope the acid changes.
Higher out, further across. Somebody should write that on a wall. Not me. I have walls to keep clean.
Both nozzles drip on the floor by the door, where they can do no harm. Try them. Then think about why they are not over there.
Paste is not clever. It goes where it is sent, as fast as it was falling. You could learn a lot from paste.
You crossed ten metres of acid on a floor I had made slippery. In any other building that would be a lawsuit.
Two pits. One island. One pad on the island, which throws you straight up and drops you back where it likes. I find that restful to watch.
The pad always drops you on the same white square. It is very strong and very stupid. You are holding something that can change what the square is.
Two pits, no swimming, and the same portal twice. You are becoming difficult to impress, which makes two of us.
The switch on the wall opens the door for three seconds. The door is at the far end. Between you and it are three presses that used to flatten sheet steel.
They still flatten things. They are not particular about what. They are also not in time with each other. Nobody here has been able to fix that, because of the flattening.
The presses are almost never all up at the same time. Almost.
Three seconds was plenty. I said it would be. I did not say it to you, but I said it.
The plate with the amber ring is on a relay. When the weight comes off it, the door stays open for three more seconds. Three. I was feeling generous.
The door wants both plates. The plain one across the acid does not wait for anybody. Neither do I, as a rule.
Three seconds is not long enough to do anything you should have done before. It is just long enough to regret it.
Three seconds, and you had most of them to spare. Do not look so pleased. The offices are empty. Nobody saw.
The panel spends three seconds in each place. You spend a little under one second falling. I will let you do the arithmetic. You have nothing else on.
You caught a moving wall twice, once with a crate. Most subjects only manage it the other way round.
The door wants the crate. The crate is coming with you. I did not say it would enjoy it.
You are falling in circles. Some of my best subjects ended up doing that. Most of them are still at it.
Seventy metres a second, with luggage. You have never been more streamlined. Or more like a projectile.
